small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_SP (e.g. 256) paired with BLOCK_OC=32 or 64, since POH*POW=4032 is huge and OC=128 is small — most of the parallelism is along the spatial dim. Also try BLOCK_K=128 to amortize the weight-load overhead (K_TOTAL=576).
- Swap loop order so weights are loaded once per (oc, k) tile and reused across the 4 pool sub-positions already; consider loading the input once for the 2x2 pool window as a single contiguous gather (3xBLOCK_SP wide stripe) and reusing across the four dots to cut x_ptr loads from 4 to ~1.
- Try `tl.math.tanh` directly instead of the `(exp(2v)-1)/(exp(2v)+1)` form to reduce register pressure, and ensure the weight is laid out as [K_TOTAL, OC] (transpose at init) so `tl.dot(x^T, w)` removes the need for any inner-loop transpose.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a persistent kernel with one program per (N, OC tile) iterating over a large spatial range, keeping the weight tile resident in registers/SMEM for the whole batch's spatial sweep — weights are tiny (128×576) and currently reloaded per spatial tile.
- Switch to channels-last (NHWC) input layout (permute once at forward entry, or store conv weights as [KH,KW,IC,OC]) so the GEMM-K dimension (IC) is the contiguous axis; this gives fully coalesced loads in the K loop and lets BLOCK_K=IC=64 with no masking.
- Fuse the 2x2 average-pool into the GEMM by computing 4 output pixels per spatial lane and reducing in registers, but share the input gather: load a (KH+1)×(KW+1) input patch once per (oc, sp) tile and accumulate into a single pooled output, eliminating 3 of the 4 redundant x-loads.
